newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway to resume foreign currency purchases.
newsitem.headline: Norway to resume foreign currency purchases.

text.p: Norway's central bank, Norges Bank, said on Thursday it would resume foreign currency purchases for the government Petroleum Fund.
The bank said foreign currency equivalent to about three billion crowns would be purchased per month during the remainder of 1997.
But, it said, it would the foreign currency purchases in response to changes in petroleum revenue flows.

Oil-rich Norway expects to have a budget surplus of 55.4 billion crowns in 1997, all of which will be placed in the Petroleum Fund for investment. Deposits into the fund are place in a Norwegian crown account in Norges Bank, which is charged with converting the amounts into foreign currency and investing overseas.
The bank said that in the period to January 10, it had bought foreign exchange for 31 billion crowns, leaving 24.4 billion crowns still to be purchased for transfer into the fund.
In addition, foreign currency corresponding to 1.2 billion would be bought and transferred into the government Petroleum Insurance Fund, it said.

"The purchases must be seen against a background of Norges Bank's role as manager of the Petroleum Fund and, as such, the purchases are not undertaken as exchange market interventions," a statement said.
